item.title: Batman actor Ben Affleck has slammed Warner Bros. for how they handled the production of Justice League and called the experience the lowest post of his career.
item.description:
Batman actor Ben Affleck has slammed Warner Bros. for how they handled the production of Justice League and called the experience the lowest post of his career.
When speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, Affleck was asked about his canceled standalone Batman film, which would've featured Joe Manganiello as Deathstroke. The actor/director said he was excited by what he was cooking up for that Batman film, but admitted that the experience of working on Justice League turned him off to the idea of having to helm a movie in the DC universe.
"The truth is, the experience of Justice League was so, so negative for lots of different reasons," said Affleck. "Some of which having to do with where I was personally, some of which having to do with the tragedy that happened during the time, and also the fact that I really saw how not to make a movie like that when the studio is at odds with the filmmaker. You're really making a mistake. That was what really doomed that."
Affleck is referencing the fact that WB battled director Zack Snyder pretty heavily on his DC films, most notably Justice League after Batman v Superman failed to meet critical expectations. The film was also deemed a bit of a disappointment by WB for not cracking the $1 billion mark, despite featuring three of DC's biggest heroes. As a result, there was a lot of pressure on Snyder to make Justice League more appealing via a lighter tone and different story ideas.
Unfortunately, Snyder had to leave the project during post-production after his daughter took her own life. Warner Bros. then enlisted the help of Avengers director Joss Whedon to come in and direct reshoots, which massively changed the film's tone and story. The reshoots were also hampered by allegations of actors being mistreated by Whedon and other issues, which Affleck stated he was aware of second-hand. He also went on to say that he believes WB used the tragedy in Snyder's family to as an "excuse" to hijack Justice League. He noted that the experience of these reshoots was the "low point" of his career.
"The way in which that was, I thought frankly, used as an excuse was one of the sh**tiest things I'd ever seen," said Affleck. "It was so gross. And then the whole environment and vibe, much of which I wasn't privvy to, but that I sort of heard about second hand in terms of Ray [Fisher] and Gal [Gadot] and other peoples' experiences. It was just like 'Wow, this is about as gross as it gets.'"
Affleck's experience on Justice League was also intertwined with a divorce and issues with alcoholism, leading to a turbulant time for the actor. He eventually stepped down away from the role of Batman and decided not to direct his own Batman film, instead passing the baton over to director Matt Reeves and actor Robert Pattinson. He eventually returned to the role for The Flash, as well as new scenes at the end of Zack Snyder's Justice League, a director's cut of the embattled film.
Zack Snyder also recently stated that a former WB executive expressed regret over how everything was handled. Some hardcore fans have held out hope that maybe one day Snyder's vision will be completed with another Justice League movie, but given how chaotic and negative the experience was for everyone involved, it seems hard to imagine it actually happening.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Chandler Riggs, best known for playing Carl in The Walking Dead, made his own fan film adapting an iconic moment from Resident Evil 7 — and he’d love to collaborate with Zach Cregger on another movie in the RE universe, if he’s up for it.
item.description:
Chandler Riggs, best known for playing Carl in The Walking Dead, made his own fan film adapting an iconic moment from Resident Evil 7 — and he’d love to collaborate with Zach Cregger on another movie in the RE universe, if he’s up for it.
Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil adaptation hit theaters in September to rave reviews, becoming the most financially successful film in the entire franchise. Just a month later, Riggs is releasing his own Resident Evil short film further along in the games’ timeline in Resident Evil 7: Biohazard.
Riggs adapted the iconic garage fight between Ethan Winters and Jack Baker in a high-octane 20-minute journey, not for fame and acclaim, but merely for the love of the game. Riggs told us that he simply wanted to bring this moment to life on-screen — but given the timing of his film and Cregger’s Resident Evil movie, we had to ask about his thoughts on how close his project was to Cregger’s big-budget take on Capcom’s flagship horror franchise.
“We were in pre-production when the article came out that Zack Cregger was going to do his [movie]. I was like, ‘Oh man, all right, we got to get ours out first.’ We were trying to beat the clock and get it out about a month ago, but parts just didn't align that way,” he explained.
“I've been looking forward to [Cregger’s RE movie] for so long,” he added. “And I mean, one of the big reasons I even made this is, you know, I was just dying to see a good, true-to-the-game live-action adaptation of Resident Evil. I cannot wait to see the new one.”
Cregger’s Resident Evil flick was widely well-received, but it has proven divisive among hardcore fans who wished to see a 1:1 adaptation of the games. Cregger was adamantly against doing this, believing the games already told their stories perfectly — and given that Riggs plays the famously faceless Ethan Winters in his own fan film, he was well-aware of how fans might feel about his own take on the source material.
“Look, it's impossible to please everybody, you know?” he admitted. “I think there's always going to be a crowd that is unhappy, but I think that it's a great way to try to get more people into the series, into the franchise, and tell a story that you want to tell. It is not an easy thing; doing a Resident Evil film with Leon and Jill and everyone, that’s a tall order, you know what I mean? Those characters are so iconic from the games, and it's not an uneasy thing to do. So I totally respect going your own direction and doing your own thing.
“It was absolutely an intimidating thing,” he said of playing Ethan Winters, whose face is shown throughout his film. “We're trying to do so much else super faithful and true to the game, but this is a huge aspect that we are breaking from it. But there isn't really another good way to tell [the story] in a live-action format. I was going back and forth like ‘Okay, could we do first person the whole time? Could we avoid getting his face in or anything?’ But the more we went back and forth on it, the more I was like, ‘I mean, if we are going to do this and are going to appeal to a wider audience — more than just the people who played the games — then we're going to have to break those rules. It was very intimidating. Hopefully people are okay with it.”
Riggs is a massive Resident Evil fan, and his fan film is proof of this. Of course, he admitted that he’d love the chance to make a feature-length movie adapting RE7 someday — as well as the chance of working with Zach Cregger on another RE movie, if the director is willing to return to the franchise.
“A huge reason for me even doing this in the first place is that I love being on set and collaborating with cool people, and that's all it is at the end of the day,” he told us. “And just because I want to be on set more, and if I can't be on set doing more films or TV shows or whatever else, then I'll just make it myself. I'll just make it happen. And that's a huge proponent of this. So, if [Cregger] wants to continue in the universe, I'm all for it. Listen, my phone is open. Hit my line!”
It’s possible that this never happens, though, given that Cregger has said he’s never touching a franchise film again due to the strong negative response he received from a vocal portion of the Resident Evil fanbase. That being said, he already has ideas for a sequel, so there’s no telling where the future of RE’s film adaptations lie.
Riggs’ Resident Evil fan film hits the internet on October 14, starring Chandler Riggs as Ethan Winters, Jason Douglas as Jack Baker, Mary Rachel Quinn, Eugenie Bonderant, Johnathan O’Niel, and Sam Coyles.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Get an exclusive look at the live-action Street Fighter movie costumes for Dhalsim, E. Honda, and Zangief in Street Fighter 6, plus a free Zangief costume code.
item.description:
The new Street Fighter movie is just days away, and to celebrate, Capcom is releasing a slew of new Street Fighter 6 costumes tied to the film’s release.
The reveals are part of an online scavenger hunt, where a series of movie-related costumes are being unveiled in various places. Guile and M. Bison costumes have already been revealed, and more costumes will be revealed throughout the month.
First up is Dhalsim, who will be played in the new movie by Vidyut Jammwal.
Next, we have a look at E. Honda, portrayed in the film by Hirooki Goto.
Finally, we can reveal the costume for Zangief, played in the movie by Borderlands’ Olivier Richters.
Along with these exclusive images, IGN can reveal the code you can use to redeem your movie-inspired Street Fighter 6 Zangief costume.
You can claim your Zangief code, which is valid across all platforms, starting on October 16. After you do, be sure to check out the Street Fighter movie, which is opening the same day only in theaters.
The Dhalsim and E. Honda costume codes will be revealed soon, so be sure to keep your eyes peeled.
For more IGN Fan Fest, be sure to check out IGN’s website, YouTube, and social channels throughout the week for more than 90 exclusive reveals across games, movies, TV, comics, and collectibles. item.title: Universal has revealed first-look pictures of Miami Vice '85 showing Michael B. Jordan as Ricardo Tubbs and Austin Butler as James 'Sonny' Crockett.
item.description:
Universal has revealed first-look pictures of Miami Vice '85 showing Michael B. Jordan as Ricardo Tubbs and Austin Butler as James 'Sonny' Crockett.
The reboot for the classic '80s show, which has been in the works from Top Gun: Maverick director Joseph Kosinski since last year, eased movie fans into Monday with two photos of its stars ahead of its release in 2028. These first photos show Jordan and Butler as their slick title characters, guns in hand.
Both images were shared on social media to celebrate the start of production, meaning there's still plenty of work to do to bring it all together before its big premiere in a few years. You can see both Jordan as Tubbs and Butler as Crockett below.
Michael B. Jordan is Tubbs. Austin Butler is Crockett. Miami Vice ’85 - now in production. https://t.co/IU9s8neqVF
Per Variety, a description for Miami Vice '85 says the reboot will explore "the glamour and corruption of mid-80's Miami." Its story is "inspired by the pilot episode and first season of the landmark television series that influenced culture and set the style of everything from fashion to filmmaking."
Despite being nearly two years away from speeding onto movie screens, this latest swing at a Miami Vice movie has amassed quite the cast. The Odyssey and original Miami Vice show star John Leguizamo was reportedly cast as the new film's main villain back in September. Fallout and The White Lotus actor Walton Goggins was reportedly added as a second villain just a few weeks ago.
Miami Vice '85 is set to premiere May 19, 2028. It's produced by Kosinski and Dylan Clark (The Batman), with Dan Gilroy and Eric Singer attached as writers.
For more, you can read up on the 2006 movie starring Colin Farrell and Jamie Foxx. IGN gave it an 8/10 review back at the time of its release, saying, "for those seeking an intense, seductive and gritty crime drama, Miami Vice delivers the goods."
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Movie retailer Zavvi has entered administration, a legal concept similar to bankruptcy, and has warned customers not to place new orders.
item.description:
Movie retailer Zavvi has entered administration, a legal concept similar to bankruptcy, and has warned customers not to place new orders.
Zavvi was an entertainment retailer, similar to FYE, in the UK during the late 2000s, which shut down all of its physical stores. However, the brand stayed alive via a website which was well-respected by physical media collectors. Zavvi has long carried a large collection of Blu-rays and 4K movies, including sought after steelbooks. Unfortunately, the website appears to be on death's door.
Zavvi has announced that it is entering administration. As a result, it will not be able to fulfill outstanding orders and preorders, and the company has told customers to speak with their banks to get their money back. Additionally, although the website remains active, the company is warning customers not to make any new purchases either.
Administration doesn't mean that Zavvi will die forever. It's a process that attempts to give companies a path back to sustainability. However, it remains to be seen if that will happen for Zavvi. If the company can't get out of this, it will be a blow to physical media lovers. The options for purchasing new Blu-rays and steelbooks have shrunk radically over the last six years or so. Major retailers like Target and Best Buy no longer sell films in-store and enthusiast websites like Zavvi are now at risk of ceasing to exist.

item.title: He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction has a release date: February 4, 2027.
item.description:
He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction has a release date: February 4, 2027.
Bitmap Bureau, the developer behind Terminator 2D: No Fate, worked with Mattel and the retro team at Clear River Games on the old-school brawler, which launches digitally and physically on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. Two physical versions of the game will be available via Limited Run Games. The standard physical release costs $29.99, and the Collector’s Edition costs $99.99.
Dragon Pearl of Destruction is inspired by the much-loved ‘80s animated series, and you can see that come through in pixel-art and 2D gameplay. The playable characters are He-Man, She-Ra, Man-At-Arms, and Teela, and you can play solo or co-op (two-player local co-op).
There are 13 stages, including the Royal Palace, the Vine Jungle, and Snake Mountain, and famous villains such as Skeletor, Evil-Lyn, Beast Man, and Trap Jaw. You’ll also bump into the dark sorceress Shokoti and the Shadow Beasts.
The Collector’s Edition includes lunchbox style packaging, pin badges, a mini-power sword, and an acrylic standee featuring He-Man riding Battle Cat, among other things. The contents of both physical editions are detailed below.
We previewed He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction in August and thought it could be the first ever good He-Man game. It comes following the release of Amazon’s Masters of the Universe, which struggled at the box office but found success on Prime Video.

item.title: Eric Barone, aka ConcernedApe, has discussed the difference between his all-conquering indie game Stardew Valley and his hotly anticipated follow-up, Haunted Chocolatier.
item.description:
Eric Barone, aka ConcernedApe, has briefly discussed the difference between his all-conquering indie game Stardew Valley and his hotly anticipated follow-up, Haunted Chocolatier.
Barone announced Haunted Chocolatier back in 2021, but amid ongoing work on his phenomenally successful Stardew Valley, progress on the follow-up has been slow going. Indeed, in June, Barone admitted to feeling somewhat embarrassed to have to keep on saying he was still working away on the game. “Feels kinda dumb posting this same thing over and over, but that’s the reality,” he said at the time.
In a new interview with GQ (thanks, Eurogamer), Barone touched on what to expect from Haunted Chocolatier when it eventually comes out, and it sounds more different from Stardew Valley than I had expected. It’s set in a more “metaphysical” locale, for a start, and in terms of gameplay it’s more of an action RPG.
“It is still what I call a town game,” Barone said, “But it’s more of an action RPG — the main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights. It's for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines. That's what I do, honestly.”
In June, Barone admitted fussing over every last detail in a bid to make Haunted Chocolatier as close to perfect as humanly possible. “I am being very thoughtful about every aspect of the game,” he said at the time. “The things in the game which the player will be interacting with or using very often need to be ‘perfect.’ They need to be seamless, clear, intuitive, satisfying, aesthetic.”
He used the example of iterating on the recipe book for making chocolates, which sounded like a significant challenge.
“To me, it’s not a simple task, as I torture myself over every last detail,” he said. “This is a UI you will be using fairly often, so it has to be perfect. You need to be able to accomplish your goal with the minimal number of clicks. There needs to be just the right amount of data presented to the player: not so much as to be overwhelming, but not so little as to be trivial or mundane. And the way that this data is laid out on the page is crucial… If the data is all clustered together, it will be disgusting to look at. The data needs to be grouped into compelling, intuitive and easy to read/understand groupings. It needs to look appealing and intriguing. And this is just the bare minimum, that players will likely take for granted. If all of that is accomplished then the player is now comfortable while perusing the recipe book. But I want more than just comfort. I want to delight the player. All of this typically requires me to iterate on something several times before I’m satisfied with it.”
Barone also explained why he didn't want to show Haunted Chocolatier off too much at this stage of development. “Partly, it feels like I’m serving a half-baked bread. I would rather serve a fully baked bread,” he said. “Also, I know that many parts of the game will likely evolve and change before release, so if I reveal them early, I risk disappointing players if the final product does not match their expectation. Fortunately, I’m in a position where I don’t need to market the game, so I can take my preferred approach.”
Haunted Chocolatier is so far without a release date, as is Stardew Valley 1.7 update, which Barone isn’t working on directly. Earlier this year, he explained his current way of working in an interview with IGN.
“Well, part of the reason why I've expanded my team a little bit is so that hopefully I can spend more time working on Haunted Chocolatier," he told us in February. "And it's worked out pretty well so far, I would say. On 1.7, the approach we're taking is that I am like, you might say the creative director and I'm involved with like, 'Okay, here's what we're going to do. Here's some of the ideas.' Then I let the team work on that. And then meanwhile, I'm working on Haunted Chocolatier.
"At some point in 1.7's cycle, I will get heavily involved, because I feel like my hand needs to touch every part of the game, every aspect of the update. I need to go over it and adjust it or at least approve everything. So it will require a lot of my time anyway, but I think the balance has been a little bit more shifted, so that I can spend more time focused on Haunted Chocolatier. And I think it's been working out pretty good. That's been a big change from the 1.3 update or 1.1 or something where it's completely me. I had no time to work on a new game. So that has changed.
"It is difficult because it's hard to shift gears, I guess. If I'm thinking about Haunted Chocolatier, it's difficult to be like, 'Okay, I'm going to one day of the week or two days of the week work on Stardew Valley.' That's not how my brain works. I'm all in one thing or the other. So I've been trying to work on that. I feel like it requires a lot of discipline, which I'm always working to improve on."
We interviewed ConcernedApe and chatted about topics such as the addition of two new marriage candidates with 1.7, the one secret players still haven't found yet, and why there isn't a Stardew Valley TV show yet. We also chatted with the Stardew Valley community about what the game has meant to them over the years.

item.title: Warhammer 40,000 maker Games Workshop has found itself in the news for its falling share price, which has left some wondering what’s going on behind the scenes.
item.description:
Warhammer 40,000 maker Games Workshop has found itself in the news for its falling share price, which has left some wondering what’s going on behind the scenes.
Games Workshop is one of the UK's biggest success stories, with its stock rising more than 70% over the past five years. But its share price has fallen 13.76% over the past six months, wiping hundreds of millions of pounds off the value of the company. This comes even as Games Workshop reports record profits. So, what’s going on?
Broadly speaking, there seems to be investor nervousness at Games Workshop’s ability to keep growing in the face of rising manufacturing and logistics costs. Some on the internet will say the recently released 11th edition of flagship tabletop wargame Warhammer 40,000 hasn’t done as well as Games Workshop had hoped, but there is no official data to back this claim up. Indeed, in an update issued mid-September, Games Workshop said that trading to August 30 was “in line with the Board’s expectations for the current financial year.”
However, there is certainly a feeling that Games Workshop may have hit a wall in terms of the popularity of its tabletop games, particularly Warhammer 40,000, which has seen multiple new, pricey miniatures released recently amid claims of over-saturation.
Things ramped up last week with two reports from the financial press about the state of Games Workshop. The first, from the Financial Times, titled ‘Is Warhammer still winning?’ The FT pointed out that while GW’s financials are, broadly speaking, very positive, retail growth per store turned negative for the first time since the pandemic in the second half of its 2026 financial year.
Then there was a report in The Times titled, ‘Games Workshop takes a hammering after mystery report.’ This story claimed a confidential Dragoneye document had wiped £480 million (approx. $635 million) off the company’s value “as the closely guarded contents trigger unease among investors.”
What’s in this Dragoneye document? We don’t know, but The Times said it was about the potential for slowing growth at Games Workshop. It’s interestingly timed, and Dragoneye is a short-focused research firm, so its report should be read with that in mind. Through it all is the obvious point that projecting a slowdown in consumer spending on Games Workshop products shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone. The global economy is struggling, the rising cost of living has caused many to rethink their spending, and AI has everyone spooked about jobs.
So, while some fans are taking to subreddits to express concern about the future of Games Workshop, there is nothing here to indicate the company is in any sort of trouble. Quite the opposite. And let’s not remember what’s in the works for Warhammer. Big hitting video games such as Total War: Warhammer 40,000 and Space Marine 3 are due out in the coming years, and Henry Cavill is soldiering on with his Warhammer 40,000 Cinematic Universe for Amazon. The entertainment push to broaden the appeal of the Warhammer 40,000 IP is surely going to stand Games Workshop in good stead over the years.
And, at the time of this article’s publication, Games Workshop’s share price was up 1.22%. The Emperor, it seems, protects.
Photo by Matthew Lloyd/Getty Images.

item.title: Gears of War: E-Day suffered a DDoS attack over the weekend, developer The Coalition has said.
item.description:
Gears of War: E-Day suffered a DDoS attack over the weekend, developer The Coalition has said.
Players suffered intermittent disconnects and login issues while trying to play the Xbox Series X and S and PC action game, which The Coalition eventually got on top of. It has now confirmed the problems were the result of a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack targeting online services.
“Our teams are continuing to monitor and mitigate this activity. We’ll provide updates if there are any significant changes,” The Coalition said. “Thank you for your patience and understanding.”
There is a great deal of speculation online about the motivation behind hitting Gears with a DDoS attack, with some pointing to a continued online vendetta against the game for apparently being “woke.” E-Day has a “mostly positive” user review rating on Steam. Whatever the reason (there may be no overarching reason behind the DDoS attack at all), E-Day is now up and running.
Last week, Alinea Analytics' head of marketing analysis, Rhys Elliott, reported that E-Day had sold an estimated 230,000 copies in its first week in what was described as a soft start. These unofficial figures, which are not backed by data provided by Microsoft, pointed to Xbox subscription service Game Pass as cannibalizing sales.
Earlier this month, the boss of The Coalition responded to reports that staff at the studio were worried they might lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, promising the next Gears game wouldn’t take as long to make.
Eurogamer had reported on internal concern that layoffs would hit The Coalition after the release of E-Day. "The mood is certainly 'let's not celebrate the game until we're three months post launch, just in case,' which is very unusual," one source told the site. "We're just expecting the next wave [of layoffs], or being reorganized under Activision or something later this year," claimed another.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s “reset” of Microsoft’s gaming business has seen nearly 2,000 people cut already this financial year, with more to come. A number of studios have left the business or are in the process of closing down. Microsoft has also reorganized its studios, bringing Halo and Sea of Thieves developer Rare under Call of Duty developer Activision, and Grounded developer Obsidian under Fallout developer Bethesda.
Of course, Gears of War: E-Day was selected to be an Xbox Series X and S and PC game, ditching any release for a sales-boosting PS5 version. The Coalition studio head Mike Crump recently told the BBC that success for E-Day goes behind sales, saying: "We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to its limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? ...Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware.”

item.title: The GTA 6 leaker has reportedly released yet another unauthorized gameplay video, this time allegedly showing Lucia fully naked in a bid to push their crypto scheme. However, some now suspect Cyberleek is using a developer build or cheats to make Jason and Lucia naked, and that the leaked gameplay does not accurately represent GTA 6 as it will play at launch.
item.description:
UPDATE: Cyberleek has reportedly followed through on their threat to release a “Lucia closeup 4k” video, and is once again tying further leaks to crypto market cap targets, ranging from $5 million to $25 million. According to online reports, Cyberleek has threatened to release a new unauthroized GTA 6 gameplay video every day, assuming the memecoin market cap targets are met. However, the Cyberleek memecoin has crashed, with a current market cap of $2.5 million.
Fans have spent the last week calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing to the person or group's previous form when it came to cashing out in August. With GTA 6 little over a month away, it seems Cyberleek is doubling down on their crypto scheme one last time.
ORIGINAL STORY: The GTA 6 leaker has reportedly released yet another unauthorized gameplay video, this time allegedly showing Lucia fully naked in a bid to push their crypto scheme. However, some now suspect Cyberleek is using a developer build or cheats to make Jason and Lucia naked, and that the leaked gameplay does not accurately represent GTA 6 as it will play at launch.
Cyberleek had threatened to release gameplay showing Lucia fully naked if the market cap of their memecoin hit $4 million. That was achieved over the weekend. However, while the new video reportedly does show Lucia fully naked, there are a number of signs that some believe suggest Cyberleek has tinkered with the build they allegedly have access to.
One suspected telltale sign from the previous leak was that a tank was spawned into the game world, suggesting access to a dev menu of some kind. Now, with two leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked but NPCs in the game world failing to react to that in any way, some believe this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats.
One theory is that Cyberleak was able to access this state for both Lucia and Jason because in at least one mission players will see both characters naked, perhaps in a nudist resort. As it stands, this is all speculation, and it is unknown if GTA 6 will feature either character naked at any point — officially at least.
Cyberleek has doubled down on their crypto scheme in the last week, threatening Rockstar and parent company Take-Two with the release of a full playthrough of the game’s story if they fail to release GTA 6 on-disc and issue a public apology — and the market cap of their memecoin hits $30 million. Of course, few believe these GTA 6 leaks are about campaigning for physical media — rather they're about making money from cryptocurrency.
To that end, Cyberleek has polled people on the release of a “Lucia closeup 4k video,” which suggests further leaks are incoming.
A cryptocurrency market capitalization (market cap) is the total dollar value of all the coins or tokens of a digital asset currently in circulation. At the time of this article’s publication, Cyberleek had a market cap of $2.7 million, having spiked at $8.4 million on October 11 as people pushed for the release of the latest gameplay. It seems unlikely that it will get anywhere near $30 million.
Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Rockstar parent company Take-Two. The company issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. But Cyberleek reemerged last week with the release of a 24-minute GTA 6 gameplay video that showed cutscenes, story beats, playable characters Jason and Lucia naked (in the case of Jason, full-frontal nudity), and a first-person camera.
It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. This week’s developments suggest Cyberleek remains at large and defiant in the face of potential legal action.
In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks, describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.
Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out," earning around $270,000 in the process. Every video posted by Cyberleek pointed to a website where fans could pay to vote on further leaks using the leaker's own cryptocurrency. Such a poll is reportedly live on Cyberleek's website now, suggesting yet another leak is on the way.
Whether the culprit or culprits are ever caught may rest on how successful Take-Two's legal team and the relevant authorities are at forcing social networks or crypto exchanges to divulge any personal details they hold on those responsible.

item.title: Doom 2016 Composer Mick Gordon Says "F##k AI"
item.description:
Aussie composer Mick Gordon is highly regarded for his experimental approach to musical composition. For 2013's Killer Instinct he employed a kangling, a Tibetan instrument traditionally carved into a human femur or tibia, to build a theme for the skeletal Spinal character out of actual bones. For 2016's Doom he famously sampled real chainsaw noises to pull off the unique guitar riffs that elevated the game's soundtrack into a heavy metal masterpiece.
However, when asked if he's considered incorporating any form of generative AI into his creative process, Gordon doesn't mince his words. To paraphrase the late Meatloaf, Gordon will do anything to create a great soundtrack, but he won't do that.
"F**k AI," said Gordon, during an interview with IGN at PAX Australia 2026.
Gordon can next be heard in Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 when it's released on October 14, since he's contributed another bone-shattering banger to score the first-person shooter's final boss fight (which you can get a taste of in the trailer below). He's also still hard at work on the soundtrack to Defect, the cyberpunk-themed squad-shooter that's being developed by a team composed of veterans of the Doom and Call of Duty games. Fans can rest assured that in both instances, Gordon's music is coming straight from the metal-loving maestro's mind (and fingers) rather than the result of a ChatGPT prompt.
"Generative AI is always going to be behind where humans are because it's going to be inherently trained off stuff that humans have already created," explained Gordon. "It creates a large database of what [it's] been trained on, and then it draws a very logical conclusion on whatever that dataset is. It's always going to be limited by its dataset, though. It's never going to be in a state where it's going to predict the next thing, the new thing, whatever humans can come up with. It's always going to be behind just by the nature of the way that these things work."
Gordon remains optimistic that audiences are always going to be drawn to the work of other humans, rather than machines.
"Humans are always going to want to interact with other humans. Always," said Gordon. "And I feel this AI stuff is just giving people more reason to abandon this digital infection that we have with our lives now."
"I feel that humans are always going to chase that human connection."
UK-based fans of Gordon's work will be able to make a human connection with the man himself when he takes the stage as the headline act at 2027's RADAR festival, where he is set to perform music from his Doom and Doom Eternal soundtracks live with a full band for the very first time.
Tristan Ogilvie is a senior video editor at IGN based in Sydney, Australia. He has 25 years of experience covering video games, having served as Deputy Editor on Official PlayStation 2 Magazine Australia and as Editor of Official Xbox 360 Magazine Australia, before joining IGN in 2009. item.title: Mick Gordon, the legendary Aussie composer who brought a headbang to every headshot in 2016's Doom and its 2020 follow-up Doom Eternal, has told IGN that he's open to the idea of contributing to future instalments in id Software's iconic shooter series.
item.description:
Mick Gordon, the legendary Aussie composer who brought a headbang to every headshot in 2016's Doom and its 2020 follow-up Doom Eternal, has told IGN that he's open to the idea of contributing to future instalments in id Software's iconic shooter series.
During an interview conducted at this weekend's PAX Australia, Gordon seemed to indicate that his involvement with Doom isn't necessarily done for good, despite the very public falling-out that occurred between the composer and Doom Eternal's development team in the wake of its release.
"There are a lot of dominoes that would have to fall in a very specific way for that to occur," said Gordon. "If those dominoes ever fell in that way, I would. Of course. Within a heartbeat."
Gordon didn't elaborate on exactly what those "dominoes" might be, but it's possible that disputes between the composer and Doom Eternal's executive producer Marty Stratton have yet to be fully resolved. In a lengthy 2022 post on Medium, Gordon accused developer id Software of failing to pay him for half of his work on the Doom Eternal soundtrack, and singled out Stratton as being a recurringly abusive presence throughout his work on the score and the OST. However, it certainly seems as though the experience hasn't dimmed Gordon's love for Doom itself.
"I had a whole list of ideas where I wanted to go with Doom," explained Gordon. "And I'd love to explore that one day, for sure."
What the future of Doom looks like with or without Gordon's involvement is another story. id Software was one of the many studios heavily impacted by Microsoft's ongoing cuts to its Xbox business, with 136 members of staff at the Doom developer affected by layoffs in July. At the time, lead services programmer Chris Hays was quoted as saying, "It's hard to make a game that is AAA, that's like we've done before, with half the people. And by hard, I mean impossible."
In the meantime, Gordon has been keeping busy with a variety of projects. He's contributed the theme music for the final boss fight in Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2, which will be released on October 14. He's also still actively at work producing the full soundtrack for Defect, the squad-based cyberpunk shooter developed by veterans of Doom and the Call of Duty series. In 2027, he's set to return to Doom at least in a performance sense, as the headliner at the UK's RADAR music festival where he'll be performing the music he composed for Doom and Doom Eternal with a full live band for the first time.

item.title: Artemis Fowl is coming back to TV screens in the form of an animated show on Disney Channel and Disney+.
item.description:
Artemis Fowl is coming back to TV screens in the form of an animated show on Disney Channel and Disney+.
Author Eoin Colfer announced that Disney had greenlit another series project based on his family fantasy novels at the 25 Years of Artemis Fowl panel at New York Comic Con 2026. He'll remain involved in the animated show as an executive producer, too, with Disney promising that he'll bring "his creative vision to dig deeper into the characters and lore of the beloved book series that is celebrating its 25th anniversary of the first book this year."
Joining Colfer in the executive producing category is Marvel's Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur's Ben Juwono, as well as DuckTales' Colleen Evanson. In a statement, the Artemis Fowl author said he is "proud and delighted to be part of the formidable team that is putting the Artemis Fowl animation on screen."
"Everyone is so talented and so positive that I feel certain the fairy world is in excellent hands," he added.
The Artemis Fowl animated series has no release date, but when it does eventually arrive, it won't be the first swing at the property to land on Disney+. In 2020, Disney launched a live-action movie with the same name, though it largely failed to leave a good impression on fans or critics. As recorded by review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, the straight-to-streaming film only whipped up a "rotten" 8% from critics and 19% from audiences.
The Artemis Fowl movie starred Ferdia Shaw as its title character and also featured appearances from Lara McDonnell, Josh Gadd, and Michael Rouse. IGN called it "an empty science fantasy tale with forgettable characters and an uninspired story" in our 4/10 review. In other words, a crack at a film didn't quite pan out, but where the 2020 project failed, the new animated show hopes to succeed.
"The action-adventure fantasy series Artemis Fowl follows 13-year-old genius Artemis Fowl as he uncovers an underground world of armed and dangerous — and surprisingly high-tech — fairies as he launches a plan to capture one and steal its magic to heal his dying mom and save his family," a description said.
The original Artemis Fowl book was published in 2001, with the rest of Colfen's stories in the universe boasting more than 35 million copies sold across the globe. Elsewhere at NYCC 2026, we got another solid look at both Godzilla Minus Zero and Blade Runner 2099. More Naruto was confirmed to be on the way, too.

item.title: Resident Evil beat Weapons to become Zach Cregger's highest-grossing film while The Social Reckoning bombed at the box office.
item.description:
Resident Evil beat Weapons to become director Zach Cregger's highest-grossing film while The Social Reckoning bombed at the box office.
The live-action adaptation of Capcom's classic survival horror series turned heads as it reached an estimated worldwide total of $320.2 million over the weekend. With $138.5 million domestically and $181.7 million internationally, Resident Evil has officially cleared Weapons' $270 million with a few weeks and change to spare.
Cregger brought his re-imagined Raccoon City to the big screen on September 18, 2026, making this weekend its fourth in theaters. The massive jump – which saw it return to the number one spot, globally – was largely propelled by its premiere in China. Of the whopping $62.65 million it accumulated through weekend four, $40.6 million was earned in China alone. Its victory over Weapons already seemed secure, but as it stands atop Cregger's catalog, it's also continuing to leave its reported $75 million budget in the dust.
Resident Evil's ongoing success in theaters kicked off when it brought in $108.3 million in its opening weekend. It was a strong start that even managed to bleed over into the gaming world with increased sales for some of the games, too, with Cregger's latest also landing as the highest-rated video game adaptation of all time.
It's hard to imagine the film's release going any better than it did, especially considering the months leading up to its premiere were plagued by negativity online. Gaming fans spent much of their time talking about the movie's lack of recognizable characters and its tweaks to the lore, with Cregger arguing that he made the changes in order to make a better movie. By just about every measure, it seems the bet paid off.
These mid-October box office results show signs of an audience ready for Halloween, with Other Mommy also performing well despite poor reviews from both critics and audiences alike (via Rotten Tomatoes). Sitting with an abysmal 18% critic score and 47% audience score, Jessica Chastain's new horror movie landed in second place globally with 45.19 million (27.5 million domestically, $17.69 million internationally).
As bone-chilling trailers convinced scary movie fans to show up for an unnerving performance, there were also some notable losers in theaters, too. Tom Cruise's Digger continued its unfortunate run with $9.6 million in weekend two, marking a 48% drop for a total of $35.3 million. The true disappointment, though, was Aaron Sorkin's The Social Network sequel, The Social Reckoning.
Starring Jeremy Allen White and Mikey Madison, and including Jeremy Strong's performance as Mark Zuckerberg, the film's opening weekend saw it open in seventh place with just $9 million. At $5.5 million domestically and $17.69 million internationally on a reported budget of $30 million (via Variety), The Social Reckoning is a certified bomb.
It's a painful reality for the Facebook movie follow-up, especially after Jesse Eisenberg's original picture ended its run with $224.9 million (via Box Office Mojo) and plenty of praise. The Social Reckoning could always stand the test of time, but with a Rotten Tomatoes score of 55% from critics and 74% from audiences, it's not looking good.
October still has plenty to give, though. Capcom's live-action Street Fighter movie and Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything will both release next weekend, October 16. DC body horror movie Clayface then follows October 23.
For the movies you can see in theaters now, be sure to check out IGN's reviews. We called Resident Evil "Great" with an 8/10 and Other Mommy "Bad" with a 4/10. We talked about the highs and lows of Digger in our 6/10 review for the Cruise film, while The Social Reckoning returned a 7/10.

item.title: Call of Duty fans are torn about NetEase Games' ECC: Redline, a new FPS that many have called a "rip-off" with the power to fill the void for frustrated Warzone players.
item.description:
Call of Duty fans are torn about NetEase Games' ECC: Redline, a new FPS that many have called a "rip-off" with the power to fill the void for frustrated Warzone players.
NetEase called its new shooter a "self-developed extreme-sports tactical shooter" when revealing it just days ago. It's yet another big swing from the China-based tech company that boasts breakneck gameplay on PC via Steam and mobile devices, but in the hours since its big debut, it's also been called a "1:1 rip" of Activision's Call of Duty: Warzone, and it's not too hard to see why.
Viewers say guns look, kick, and move in a way that seems familiar, but the similarities don't stop there. Everything down the UI is being investigated by FPS enjoyers, too, with things like the sound effects also evoking the same kind of gritty action Call of Duty is known for. Even the way the first-person camera blurs when dropping from heights might feel familiar to fans of Warzone and other shooters. Even with characters that present their own unique abilities and gadgets, ECC: Redline has had a hard time escaping the comparisons online.
Introducing ECC: REDLINE, an extreme-sports tactical shooter.Welcome to the Extreme Circuit Championship.Enter the Circuit, Own the Edge.Wishlist now on Steam:https://t.co/zy0dnkBGQn#ECCREDLINE #ECC https://t.co/TL7c3fAoAX
"Warzone + Delta Force + Blood Strike = ECC: Redline," one YouTube comment left on NetEase's official upload said.
"It’s 1-to-1 Warzone, hilarious s**t," another commenter on Reddit said.
"Literally the first thing that popped into my head was wow they have no shame," another replied, "straight copied COD even down to the UI and emblems etc."
Meanwhile, Call of Duty has faced its own struggles in the six years since the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare reboot introduced Warzone in 2019. Like so many other popular ongoing FPS experiences, the battle royale offshoot's popularity has ebbed and flowed, with many of its millions of fans often still calling back to its launch build and its first map, Verdansk, as the glory days.
This looks about as close of a 1:1 rip of Warzone as someone could legally get away with
This is Warzone with player abilities and some blatant CoD rips😂
@iKaito_1 similar? its literally copy and paste
Activision has returned to Verdansk in an attempt to recapture that magic, but it's done little to calm those nostalgic for the past. As the broader Call of Duty brand goes through its own struggles, some players – even those willing to admit NetEase may have gone too far in a few places – say a polished-looking shooter like ECC: Redline could scratch a pretty specific itch. Some even believe the NetEase shooter could give Call of Duty a run for its money.
"If ECC: Redline actually has good servers, movement, AND listens to its community… COD might finally have to start trying again," one post on X/Twitter said.
"Close enough, welcome back OG Warzone," another player said, acknowledging the similarities before saying the NetEase game "looks better tbh."
Looks like someone reverse-engineered OG Warzone and added character abilities.I’m actually kinda interested in trying this 😅
Warzone don’t have ability 🥳! Netease definitely might pull this one off lol https://t.co/oHFmquZoTK
@ModernWarzone So what? I'd rather spend it on a ripoff game who listens to their customers then a conglomerate who 💩 on them.
"I LEGIT thought it was WZ at first because i didn't check the title," one social media user said, adding a crying emoji.
NetEase has faced criticism regarding its approach to previous games in the past. A less extreme example is Marvel Rivals, a comic book hero shooter that exploded with popularity – and also managed to pick up some comparisons to Blizzard Entertainment's Overwatch – when it launched in 2024. On the other hand is Hyper Front, a 5v5 tactical shooter that Riot Games launched a lawsuit against after it drew comparisons to Valorant.
ECC: Redline currently has no release date but is being billed as a free-to-play game. Warzone, meanwhile, is slated to receive a slew of new updates when Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches later this month.

item.title: Bandai Namco has revealed a first look at Tekken 8 DLC character Yujiro Hanma, and the Baki rep is looking just as uncanny as fans expected.
item.description:
Bandai Namco has revealed a first look at Tekken 8 DLC character Yujiro Hanma, and the Baki rep is looking just as uncanny as fans expected.
The new trailer for the fighting game's Season 3 characters debuted alongside Evo France 2026. Following Kunimitsu's release in June and Bob's release in August, kangaroo-and-joey fighter Roger Jr. is now officially set for a November 11 early access launch, with the full release following November 16, but the character most fans are looking forward to is still without a proper release date.
Roger Jr. is definitely the star of the new Tekken 8 DLC trailer, with nearly three minutes of its four-minute runtime dedicated to showing off the marsupial boxer's gameplay. The Yujiro teaser, meanwhile, is tucked at the end, but its reveals are particularly shocking. You can see how the Baki the Grappler villain has been reimagined within the world of Tekken below.
Yujiro is… expressive, to say the least, so nailing his face and bulging muscles was always going to draw attention. Well, the Bandai Namco team did their best, with today's Evo trailer showing just a few shots of his iconic toothy smile and flexibility.
It looks like work on the anime guest character is still underway, but just because there's no release date doesn't mean there isn't a plan to show more. The end of the new teaser promised that a new Yujiro trailer will premiere alongside the Tekken World Tour Finals January 17, 2027. That's three months out from now, so we can probably expect to see gameplay by that point.
Looking back at the calendar, Bandai Namco has typically had a few months of downtime between Tekken 8 DLC releases. It will have been two months since Roger Jr. was released when the Yujiro trailer is shared, meaning we can also expect a release date announcement around that time, too. If we're lucky, the Baki fighter might even drop that same day, but again, nothing regarding his release date has been confirmed quite yet.
Roger Jr. and Yujiro are both included in the Season 3 pass and will round out its promise of four bonus characters. Season 1 and Season 2 included fighters like Heihachi, Armor King, Anna, and Final Fantasy 16 protagonist Clive Rosfield. While passes cost $30 each, the Season 3 pass is currently available for $34.99.
IGN learned more about Yujiro's inclusion in Tekken 8 when speaking with producer Naoya Yasuda and director of promotions and former Baki manga editor Yuki Yokoi earlier this year. Be sure to read the full interview for insight into how and why the team decided to include a character that never loses. You can also read about how former Tekken director Katsuhiro Harada influenced one of Roger Jr.'s best references, and the player who climbed through the ranks while blindfolded.

item.title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls will continue its Year 1 DLC roadmap with Thor (Jane Foster) this winter, with two more characters coming in 2027.
item.description:
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls will continue its Year 1 DLC roadmap with Thor (Jane Foster) this winter, with two more characters coming in 2027.
Developer Arc System Works confirmed the lineup alongside Evo France 2026. The Jane Foster version of Asgard's God of Thunder is now officially set to follow Phoenix Cyclops after he releases November 2, 2026, with today's announcement coming with both a sneak peek at her Marvel Tokon model in Odin's Vault on Asgard.
The clip doesn't show too much, only teasing that we'll probably see Jane fight off Loki while wielding Mjolnir when a proper gameplay trailer premieres at a later date. Arc System Works said she's scheduled to launch in Marvel Tokon "winter 2027," so expect to see her arrival sometime before March of next year. Despite some concerns from players that poor sales could jeopardize the Marvel fighting game's future, at least two more characters will arrive in spring and summer 2027, too.
Yes, Spider-Man anti-hero and Symbiote menace Venom will finally join the roster in spring 2027. X-Men firecracker Jubilee will then follow in the summer of that year. While Cyclops and Thor are entering the fray as relatively lesser-known versions of themselves, Venom and Jubilee appear to be mostly straightforward.
That means Marvel Tokon players will get to see them fight the rest of the tag-team fighting with and against the game's roster – which includes characters like Doctor Doom, Iron Man, Carnage, Magneto, and more – in Arc System Works' heightened style. Although the details surrounding each DLC release are unclear, the reveal trailer did at least confirm that Venom will also come with a stage based on the Symbiote home world of Klyntar.
It's all part of the Year 1 Character and Stage Pass, which costs $34.99. A roadmap with some of the most beloved characters from Marvel history would usually be enough to have comic book and video game fans frothing at the mouth, but uncertainty surrounding the project might have some looking at the Evo announcement in a different light.
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls launched to strong reviews (a 9/10 from IGN) in August, but at least on PC, players have struggled. Its Steam launch brought mixed reviews from fans who complained of widespread technical issues and PlayStation Network requirements. Even as the developers almost immediately promised to investigate the issues, it didn't take long for the backlash to swell to the point that famed fighting game community member Maximilian Dood wrote off playing the PC version altogether.
It only took a few days for Arc System Works to push out a fix for most players' issues, but as Steam player numbers still struggle to break even 1,000 concurrent users (via SteamDB), even the developers have admitted earning back trust will be "extremely challenging." While Marvel Tokon's presence on PlayStation 5 seemed to go over well, director Kazuto Sekine eventually went on to apologize for the PC launch.
The developers clearly have a game plan for at least up until summer 2027. While we wait to see how characters like Thor, Venom, and Jubilee will punch and kick their way into Marvel Tokon, you can read about the characters dataminers were expecting to see first.

item.title: Toho's latest Godzilla Minus Zero trailer is here and puts the spotlight on King Ghidorah's lightning-like gravity beams and Godzilla's iconic atomic breath.
item.description:
Toho's latest Godzilla Minus Zero trailer is here and puts the spotlight on King Ghidorah's lightning-like gravity beams and Godzilla's iconic atomic breath.
This new sneak peek at the King of the Monsters and the latest iteration of his archnemesis debuted as part of New York Comic Con 2026. Toho refrained from showing its new design for Ghidorah yet again, but there's still plenty of new footage to see in the one-minute video.
How did Noriko Oishi (Minami Hamabe) survive Godzilla's first attack? That's the question Godzilla Minus Zero teases an answer for in its second full-length trailer. It looks like viewers are in for pure carnage this time around, as the three-headed kaiju zaps any airborne structures out of the sky left and right. You can see how the sequel's returning human crew will "fight fire with fire" next month in the trailer below.
Fight fire with fire. 🔥 #GodzillaMinusZeroGodzilla Day IMAX Early Access on November 3. In theatres November 6.Tickets on sale now.https://t.co/2Ktmma6fOa https://t.co/U0NvFbnGL9
With less than a month until its premiere, it seems the filmmakers behind the Godzilla Minus One sequel are going to save the full Ghidorah reveal for those who go to the theater. We'll at least know how the character has been redesigned for the Minus universe when it premieres November 6.
Godzilla Minus Zero's NYCC presence wasn't just limited to this electrifying new trailer, though. Producer Kazuaki Kishida, visual effects artist and compositor Tatsuji Nojima, sound designer and Foley artist Natsuko Inoue, and production and post-production sound mixer Hisafumi Takeuchi all gathered in New York for a panel covering the sequel and how it came to be. IGN attended the talk and came away with a few highlights.
Nojima, who walked away from Godzilla Minus One as the first Gen Z Oscar winner in the visual effects category, said his time working on the 2023 film started simply as a hobby before director Takashi Yamazaki took note of his abilities. Kishida joked, "I don't know if I'd have a job right now" if not for the 25-year-old VFX artist's work, but Nojima isn't the only younger member of the crew.
"There are even younger team members on the Godzilla Minus Zero team – 22, 23," Kishida said via translator. "They're talented enough to be given an entire cut or a scene to manage on their own. Director Yamazaki really likes working with young talent. I think he's very open-minded, and he absorbs whatever fresh takes or new ways younger artists are approaching different problems, and how they're solving it. There isn't really an age hierarchy in his organization. Everyone works very collaboratively, and I think it's a very good environment for young artists to try and flex what they have."
One VFX-packed scene that viewers have already caught in trailers sees Godzilla emerging from the ocean while chasing after a plane. Even short moments like this can be quite complicated to bring to life when skyscraper-sized monsters are involved. Godzilla Minus Zero's status as the first Japanese production filmed for IMAX only made the process more complex, which is why it's especially impressive that the ocean scene in question required 2 billion particles and was made by just two people.
Meanwhile, the crew had to get especially creative when trying to imagine what creatures like Godzilla and Ghidorah would sound like in real life. In Godzilla Minus One, the echo of its title kaiju's unmistakable roar was recorded by capturing audio of his voice in a baseball stadium. Introducing a new monster with Godzilla Minus Zero then took them to record audio in a dam.
"I recall there were people having a picnic, maybe people just taking a stroll," Takeuchi said. "The person walking their dog, though, they had the worst time because the dog was freaking out and barking back at us."
It'll all come together in just a few short weeks. In the meantime, you can see why IGN gave Godzilla Minus One an 8/10. We've also already got a review for Godzilla Minus Zero, and you can see why we gave it a 7/10 here.

item.title: Naruto is alive and well, as author Masashi Kishimoto has announced a new manga called Shadow Rising – and a new anime crossover series is on the way, too.
item.description:
Naruto is alive and well, as author Masashi Kishimoto has announced a new manga called Shadow Rising – and a new anime crossover series is on the way, too.
Both Naruto projects were announced during the Naruto panel at New York Comic Con 2026. Details about the manga, specifically, were light, with only Kishimoto's involvement and its "Shadow Rising" title confirmed for now.
The panel did come with more information about that anime series, though. Aptly titled "Naruto x Ninku," the show will serve as a full-on crossover between Naruto and popular '90s manga and anime franchise Ninku. Both the show and the manga did receive teaser trailers, which you can see below.
A teaser for new NARUTO manga by Masashi Kishimoto is here! Stay tuned for more updates at the NARUTO Super Stage at Jump Festa 2027!#PROJECT_RASENGAN #NARUTO #JumpFesta https://t.co/EseP4OSffI
Two legendary shinobi series collide.Fully supervised by Koji Kiriyama and Masashi Kishimoto, NARUTO x NINKŪ is in production!Director: Noriyuki AbeCharacter Designer / Chief Animation Director: Tetsuya Nishiohttps://t.co/d9fv6N2g86#PROJECT_RASENGAN #NARUTO #NINKU https://t.co/VExZf7MTeJ
"Team 7 members Naruto, Sasuke, and Sakura are given a mission by Kakashi," an official description for Naruto x Ninku said. "Since Kakashi cannot participate himself, Naruto is appointed acting leader. As a result of this decision, Naruto is fully motivated to make the mission a success. However, on the way, Team 7 finds themselves lost in another world. What appears before the bewildered trio is a boy with a face resembling a frog’s, named Fūsuke. What awaits them in this strange new world?"
Meanwhile, as reported by Variety, the Naruto panel also came with a surprise update on the live-action movie. Amid rumors of early plot details and casting decisions, director Destin Daniel Cretton shared a message where he explained "what an honor it is to bring Kishimoto-sensei's incredible world and characters to life."
"The further we get into making this film, the more excited I am about what we’re creating," he continued. "What I’ve always loved about Naruto is that he’s the character who might normally get sidelined as a sidekick. He’s excitable, he tries too hard, and people underestimate him. But he has an incredible heart. No matter how many times he fails or gets knocked down, he never stops believing in himself or fighting for the people he loves. That spirit is at the heart of the story we’re telling.
"These characters mean so much to so many people, myself included, and I carry that with me as we make this film. We’re approaching the world, relationships, and journeys Kishimoto-sensei created with a lot of care, and we want to capture what makes NARUTO so special. We’re hard at work and will have more to share soon. Until then, thank you for your passion, your patience, and for being along for the ride. I can’t wait for you to see what’s ahead!"
A description in the YouTube upload for Shadow Rising promised more details will be shared at the Naruto Super Stage at Jump Festa 2027. The Naruto x Ninku upload, meanwhile, confirmed that the show is in production with supervision from Kishimoto and Ninku author Koji Kiriyama, with the Naruto X/Twitter account confirming Noriyuki Abe as its director and Tetsuya Nishio as its character designer/chief animation director. Release date details remain a mystery for now.

item.title: Prime Video has published a new Blade Runner 2099 trailer, revealing more about the mystery surrounding its missing Replicants, as well as the roles Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh play in the story.
item.description:
Prime Video has published a new Blade Runner 2099 trailer, revealing more about the mystery surrounding its missing Replicants, as well as the roles Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh play in the story.
This more detailed look at the Amazon-backed limited series and its dystopian sci-fi setting arrived at New York Comic Con 2026. Attendees at the Blade Runner 2099 panel were treated to the new trailer in person, with both it and a new poster now available for all to see online.
Starring Schafer (Euphoria) and Yeoh (Everything Everywhere All at Once) as Cora and Olwen, respectively, Blade Runner 2099 is set to premiere in November. You can see the NYCC 2026 trailer below.
A new world. A new order. A new Blade Runner. Blade Runner 2099, a new limited series, premieres November 25th on Prime Video. https://t.co/03OicCMpKl
"Fifty years after the events of Blade Runner 2049, Los Angeles has been reborn, just not by humanity," an official description from Prime Video said. "Cora, a fugitive in a final bid to stop running, takes on one last identity: a Blade Runner. Forced to partner with Olwen, a Replicant days from dying, she hunts down a runaway hiding a truth that could collapse a fragile city."
Today's comic-con trailer fills in some of the blanks left by the teaser revealed at San Diego Comic-Con this past July. Set 50 years after Ryan Gosling's Blade Runner 2049 and 80 years after Harrison Ford's original movie, Yeoh's Olwen can be heard saying 10 female and 18 male Replicants have gone missing in the last year. Amid tense words from Schafer's character, viewers are told that a mysterious "he" is out there, and he "knows the cure for all Replicants."
"I don't know what you're doing," Yeoh's Olwen says as the trailer closes. "Do you?"
The Blade Runner 2099 NYCC 2026 trailer provided a closer look into a mystery that certainly looks like it will fit in with past entries, but we'll have to wait until its November 25, 2026, release date to see how all of the pieces will come together. Its binge release plan will see all eight episodes available to stream on the same day.
With both Ridley Scott's '80s original film and Denis Villeneuve's legacy sequel enjoying a dedicated following to this day, there's already a lot of hype behind Blade Runner 2099. For more while we wait, you can read IGN's new NYCC interview with showrunner Silka Luisa.
